(p-47) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿A soul will know what it has sent forward and left behind﴾. This is the answer to the statement. We have explained it in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Man will be informed on that Day of what he sent forward and left behind﴾ [al-Qiyāmah: 13].

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O mankind﴾. Concerning it there are four sayings.

One: it refers to Abu al-Ashaddayn, who was a disbeliever. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil. We have mentioned his name in [al-Muddaththir: 30].

The second: it is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, said by ʿAṭāʾ.

The third: Ubayy ibn Khalaf, said by ʿIkrimah.

The fourth: it points to every disbeliever, mentioned by al-Māwardī.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿What has deceived you﴾. al-Zajjāj said: that is, what has deceived you and enticed you until you neglected what was obligatory upon you? Others said: the meaning is: what has made you secure from His punishment, when He is Generous and Forgiving, since He did not punish you immediately? It was said to al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ: "If Allah, glorified is He, were to stand you on the Day of Resurrection and say: 'What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?' what would you say?" He said: "I would say: Your veils let down deceived me." Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh said: "If He said to me: 'What has deceived you concerning Me?' I would say: Your kindness, past and present." It was said: when He mentioned here the attribute which is generosity, rather than His other attributes, it was as if He had taught His servant the answer, so that he would say: "The generosity of the Generous has deceived me."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Who created you﴾ and you were not a thing, ﴿and proportioned you﴾ as a human who hears and sees (p-48) ﴿and made you balanced﴾. Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read: ﴿fa-ʿadalaka﴾ with shaddah. ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read: "fa-ʿadalaka" with no shaddah. al-Farrāʾ said: As for whoever reads it without shaddah, its meaning—and Allah knows best—is: He fashioned you into whatever form He willed, whether beautiful or ugly, tall or short. It was said: in the form of a father, in the form of an uncle, in the form of some relatives, by way of resemblance. As for whoever reads it with shaddah, he intends—and Allah knows best—that He made you upright, of balanced creation. Others said: He balanced your limbs so that no hand excels over another hand, nor a foot over another foot, and He made you equitable rather than making you a beast.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you﴾. al-Zajjāj said: it is permissible that "mā" is superfluous (zāʾidah). It is also permissible that it means the conditional and the response, so the meaning is: in whatever form He willed to assemble you in, He assembled you. Concerning the meaning of the verse there are four sayings.

One: in whatever form of the forms of relatives He assembled you, which is the meaning of the saying of Mujāhid.

The second: in whatever form, of beauty, or ugliness, or tallness, or shortness, or male, or female, which is the meaning of the saying of al-Farrāʾ.

The third: if He willed to assemble you in a form other than the human form, He would assemble you, said by Muqātil. ʿIkrimah said: if He willed, in the form of a monkey, and if He willed, in the form of a pig.

The fourth: if He willed, in the form of a human with deeds of good. And if He willed, in the form of a donkey with dullness and foolishness, and if He willed, in the form of a dog with stinginess, or a pig with gluttony. Mentioned by al-Thaʿlabī.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Nay, you deny the Religion﴾. Abū Jaʿfar read "with the yāʾ" (yukadhdhibūna), that is, the recompense and the reckoning, you claim that it will not occur. Then He informed them that their deeds are preserved, so He said (p-49) the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians﴾, that is, from the angels who guard your deeds for you, ﴿noble﴾ with their Lord, ﴿writers﴾ who write your deeds, ﴿they know what you do﴾ of good and evil, so they write it down against you.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss﴾. That is in the Hereafter when they enter Paradise. ﴿And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire﴾. Concerning the wicked there are two sayings.

One: they are the polytheists.

The second: the wrongdoers. It is reported from Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Malik that he said to Abū Ḥāzim: "I wish I knew what awaits us with Allah." He said to him: "Present your deeds to the Book of Allah, for you will know what you have with Him." He said: "Where do I find it?" He said: "At His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss﴾ ﴿And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire﴾." Sulaymān said: "Then where is the mercy of Allah?" He said: "Near to the good-doers."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They will burn therein﴾, meaning: they will enter Hellfire suffering its heat, ﴿on the Day of Recompense﴾, that is, the Day of reward for deeds, ﴿and they will not be absent from it﴾, that is, from the Fire. This indicates the eternity of the disbelievers. Some scholars permitted that "minhā" (from it) be a metaphor for the Resurrection, so the benefit of the statement would be the affirmation of the Resurrection. This includes the righteous and the wicked. Then He magnified that Day by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾ Then He repeated it to exalt its matter. Ibn al-Sāʾib used to say: the address with this is to the disbelieving human, not to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The Day when no soul will possess anything for another soul﴾. Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read "yawmu" (p-50) with a raised vowel (ḍamma), and the rest with a fatḥah. al-Zajjāj said: whoever raises "al-yawm," it is on the basis that it is an attribute of His saying "Day of Recompense." It is also permissible that its raising be by implying "huwa" (it is), and its being in the accusative on the meaning: these things mentioned will occur ﴿on a Day when no soul will possess anything for another soul﴾. The exegetes said: the meaning of the verse is that no one possesses the command except Allah, and He has not granted any of the creation possession of anything as He granted them in this world. Muqātil used to say: no soul will possess for a disbelieving soul any benefit. The unrestricted statement is more correct, because Muqātil, as I think, feared negating the intercession of the believers. Intercession only occurs by the command of Allah and His granting of possession.
